original_question: Let (f_n) be a regular polynomial sequence, meaning f_n(z)=Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n and with positive constants A1,A2,A3 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A1, |a_{n,j}|≤A2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A3 d_n. Assume the generalized Julia set J(f_n) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients in the three-term recurrence for the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that they converge to an almost periodic sequence up to an error tending to zero.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 5: the open problem asking whether the recurrence coefficients for the equilibrium measure of a real Cantor-type Julia set arising from a regular polynomial sequence are asymptotically almost periodic. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly uses the paper’s notion of a regular polynomial sequence, keeps the setting on the real line, uses the equilibrium measure on the Julia set, and asks for asymptotically almost periodic recurrence coefficients rather than the stronger autonomous almost-periodicity conjecture. That matches the scope and intent of Problem 5 in Section 3. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
missing_details: The paper defines J((f_n)) as the Julia set of the composed family F_n = f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1, via the Fatou set of normality for (F_n); your draft uses the phrase generalized Julia set without spelling this out. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The coefficients a_{n,j} should be stated to lie in C, since the paper works with complex polynomials even though the Julia set is assumed to lie in R. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

To make the recurrence part stand alone, one should specify that P_n(x;μ) are the monic orthogonal polynomials for μ = μ_{J((f_n))}, with P_{-1}≡0 and P_0≡1, satisfying xP_n(x)=P_{n+1}(x)+b_{n+1}P_n(x)+a_n^2P_{n-1}. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The paper’s phrase recurrence coefficients refers to the two sequences (a_n)_{n≥1} and (b_n)_{n≥1}; your draft does not explicitly say whether asymptotic almost periodicity is required for each sequence separately or for the coefficient pair sequence. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

Almost periodic is defined in Section 1.1 through extension to a bounded two-sided sequence whose shift orbit is precompact in l^∞(Z); your draft uses the term informally but not with the paper’s exact meaning. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

Asymptotically almost periodic should be stated as existence of an almost periodic comparison sequence with pointwise error tending to 0 as n→∞, not merely as vague convergence toward an almost periodic sequence. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The paper itself leaves Cantor-type subset of the real line undefined here; for a paper-faithful rewrite it is better to keep that exact phrase, or at most to say compact real Cantor-type Julia set, rather than replace it by a broader condition. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

Because the source is an open problem, the most faithful rewrite should be interrogative (Is it true that ...?) rather than theorem-style (Prove that ...), even though the mathematical content is otherwise the same. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
refined_question: Let (f_n)_{n≥1} be a sequence of polynomials in C[z], where f_n(z)=sum_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n, and write F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1. Assume that (f_n) is a regular polynomial sequence, i.e. there exist constants A_1,A_2,A_3>0 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A_1, |a_{n,j}|≤A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A_3 d_n for all n. Suppose that the Julia set J((f_n)) of the family (F_n) is a Cantor-type subset of R, and let μ_{J((f_n))} be its equilibrium measure. If P_n(x;μ_{J((f_n))}) denotes the monic orthogonal polynomial sequence for μ_{J((f_n))}, determined by P_{-1}≡0, P_0≡1, and xP_n(x)=P_{n+1}(x)+b_{n+1}P_n(x)+a_n^2P_{n-1}(x), is it true that both recurrence-coefficient sequences (a_n)_{n≥1} and (b_n)_{n≥1} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that each differs by o(1) from the restriction to N of a two-sided almost periodic sequence? ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
justification: This draft is aimed at Section 3, Problem 5, not at a neighboring problem. The surrounding paragraph first recalls Bellissard’s autonomous conjecture for totally disconnected real Julia sets and then the conjecture for the specific Cantor sets K(γ), before posing the nonautonomous generalization for regular polynomial sequences; that is exactly the direction of your draft. Section 1.1 supplies the paper’s precise meanings of recurrence coefficients, almost periodic, and asymptotically almost periodic, while Section 1.2 supplies the definitions of regular polynomial sequence and of the Julia set J((f_n)). No explicit equivalent reformulation is given for Problem 5 in this paper, so the safest refined version is a direct stand-alone restatement of that open problem with the nearby notation filled in. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
